narrative:
The model estimated your chance of becoming a bad credit risk at 26%. That means it saw roughly a one-in-four likelihood of serious repayment difficulty; although this is not a majority, it was above the approval limit used for this decision, so your application was denied.

The most influential information was your savings position, recorded as unknown or none. This was the strongest factor overall and it actually leaned toward good credit, so the lack of recorded savings did not by itself make you look risky. Second came your checking-account status, also recorded as none; this was the next strongest factor and again leaned toward good credit. Checking accounts with no balance or no account are common among approved applicants. The third most important factor was that you have another bank installment plan. Only about 9% of approved applicants have this, and it was the main top-ranked feature pushing toward bad credit.

The denial reflects the overall combination: your savings and checking information helped, but the existing bank installment plan added risk, and other less influential details kept the estimate above the limit. The requested 48-month term, well above the approved average of about 19 months, and the 3,914 DM amount also added upward pressure. To improve a future application, document any savings, close or reduce other installment commitments, consider shortening the requested term or reducing the amount, and ask the lender which conditions would make approval more likely.
